ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

A barrier at the ulcer surface

A patient with a duodenal ulcer receives sucralfate. Experimental examination shows the drug concentrated at the ulcer base with little systemic absorption. Which action best explains its benefit at this location?

  1. Formation of an adherent protective complex over injured mucosa
  2. Irreversible inhibition of the parietal proton pump
  3. Competitive blockade of histamine H2 receptors
  4. Neutralization of all gastric acid throughout the day
  5. Eradication of H. pylori through ribosomal inhibition
Answer and explanation

Formation of an adherent protective complex over injured mucosa

Sucralfate forms a local protective barrier at the ulcer site, limiting exposure to luminal injurious factors.

Option explanations

Formation of an adherent protective complex over injured mucosa: Sucralfate forms a local protective barrier at the ulcer site, limiting exposure to luminal injurious factors.

Irreversible inhibition of the parietal proton pump: PPIs inhibit the proton pump.

Competitive blockade of histamine H2 receptors: H2 antagonists block histamine signaling.

Neutralization of all gastric acid throughout the day: Sucralfate is not a powerful systemic or sustained acid suppressant.

Eradication of H. pylori through ribosomal inhibition: It is not an H. pylori antibiotic.
